question: Does single-forward K1 with step-wise True EMA (0.9999) and Clean-BN match or exceed mean2 accuracy at >=35% lower cost on 100K PCQM4Mv2?

hypothesis.observed_deficiency: Double-forward pass adds ~40-70% training step overhead, while training Dropout corrupts BN running statistics and lack of True EMA impairs generalization.
alternative_explanations: Single-forward loss gradient lacks stochastic second-view regularization.
True EMA requires more steps than 40 epochs to wash out initialization.
Clean-BN recalibration on 16K samples might overfit.
hypothesis.changed_mechanism: Single forward pass per step + step-wise BoundForeachEMA (decay 0.9999) + post-selection Clean-BN calibration on 16,384 training molecules.
hypothesis.cheapest_falsifier: One 40-epoch 100K PCQM4Mv2 training run evaluated on fixed 50K development set with strictly frozen seed 42 and batch size 128.
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_positive: Advance to 500K scale-up candidate under pre-registered efficiency and accuracy gates.
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_negative: Close K1 single-forward EMA route; retain mean2 or explore alternative state regularizers.
historical_unknowns: True EMA convergence curve on K1
Exact Clean-BN recovery magnitude under EMA weights
